negative: Attempt a non-lifecycle callback on a bare sequence instance.
positive: Register supported callbacks on concurrent and immediate assertions and lifecycle callbacks on sequence and property instances.

edge: Register null user data and verify it is passed unchanged.
positive: Validate all five arguments in an invoked callback.

edge: Remove after one of several attempts.
negative: Cause another event or an event on another assertion.
positive: Cause the same event multiple times and observe one invocation per occurrence, then remove the callback.

edge: Remove a successful callback between two occurrences of its selected event.
negative: Attempt an invalid assertion-callback registration and verify that it returns NULL.
positive: Register an assertion callback successfully, remove it using the returned handle, and verify later matching events do not invoke it.

edge: Use two same-named assertions in distinct instances and register on only one assertion handle.
negative: Cause the specified event on a different assertion and verify that it does not invoke the callback registered on the selected assertion.
positive: Register the same event callback on one of two assertions and verify that only the selected assertion invokes it.

edge: Run overlapping attempts and distinguish them by attemptStartTime.
positive: Run a multicycle attempt and compare start, completion, step, disabled, and control-event cb_time values with the common attemptStartTime.

edge: Use assume and cover statement handles.
negative: Apply it using a sequence or property instance handle.
positive: Apply a control using an assert-statement handle.

edge: Repeat each control.
positive: Disable during an active attempt, then enable for later attempts.

edge: Repeat each control.
positive: Disable then enable fail action around separate failures.

edge: Use identical assertion names in sibling scopes and select each by its scope handle.
negative: Look up an assertion name from a scope where that name is not visible.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Look up a named assertion relative to its containing scope.

edge: Compare handles for repeated instances generated from one declaration.
notes: A VPI consumer and multiply instantiated design are required.
positive: Obtain handles for the same assertion declaration in two module instances and distinguish their instance identities.
Lock, attempt a status change, then unlock and retry.

edge: Enable during an existing attempt and verify that attempt is unaffected, then repeat the enable control.
positive: Enable nonvacuous-success pass actions for one assertion and verify a later nonvacuous success executes its pass action.

edge: Repeat same-state control.
positive: Exercise both success kinds before, during, and after disabling pass action.

edge: Verify another assertion remains unchanged.
positive: Reset one assertion with multiple active attempts.

edge: Query an assertion inheriting its clock from context.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Query assertions clocked by an explicit clocking block and by an explicit event expression.

edge: Query corresponding assertions in two instances of the same module and distinguish the containing instance while retaining the same module definition.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Query a named assertion in a module instance and verify its name, containing instance, and module definition information.

edge: Place two assertions on one line at different columns.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Query an assertion declared at a known file location and compare all three source coordinates.

edge: Distinguish a property instance from an assert statement that uses a property.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Query static type information for one object of each listed assertion category.

edge: Disable during an existing attempt and verify that attempt is unaffected, then repeat the disable control.
positive: Disable vacuous-success pass actions for one assertion and verify a later vacuous success does not execute its pass action.

edge: Disable twice.
positive: Enable stepping for an attempt, then disable it and observe no later step callbacks.

edge: Change mode with repeated enable before start.
negative: Try to modify stepping mode after the attempt starts.
positive: Enable stepping before an identified attempt starts and observe callbacks.

edge: Compare success, failure, and step callbacks from one assertion.
negative: Expect attempt information on a lock callback.
notes: Do not inspect fields the standard does not mark valid for the event.
positive: Trigger each event family and inspect only the fields specified as valid.
Run overlapping attempts, kill one by its start time, and verify the other attempt continues while sampled history is preserved.

edge: Toggle disable iff at the attempt's starting sample.
positive: Disable one attempt at start and another during evaluation.

edge: Verify the state change is scoped to the selected assertion.
positive: Disable then enable one assertion and observe both callbacks.

edge: Cause failure after each state.
positive: Disable then enable fail action and observe both events.
Cause property failure and sequence nonmatch and observe failure callbacks.

edge: Keep a sibling assertion unlocked.
positive: Lock then unlock one assertion and observe both callbacks in order.

edge: Keep vacuous-success pass-action execution disabled while enabling only nonvacuous-success execution.
positive: Enable nonvacuous-success pass actions on one assertion and observe cbAssertionEnableNonvacuousAction.

edge: Exercise vacuous and nonvacuous success.
positive: Disable then enable pass action and observe both events.
Reset an assertion with an active attempt and observe the callback.

edge: Observe repeated starts on successive clock ticks.
negative: Register on a property instance unused by any verification statement and ensure no start event.
positive: Observe start for an instantiated property evaluation.

edge: Distinguish sequence match from property success while using the same reason.
positive: Trigger successful property and sequence evaluations and observe success callbacks.

edge: Keep nonvacuous-success pass-action execution enabled while disabling only vacuous-success execution.
positive: Disable vacuous-success pass actions on one assertion and observe cbAssertionDisableVacuousAction.

negative: Make the implication succeed nonvacuously and do not classify that result as vacuous.
positive: Make an implication succeed vacuously and observe the callback.

edge: Leave another attempt active.
positive: Kill an active multicycle attempt and observe the callback.

edge: Fail an assertion after each state change.
notes: The source describes success categories for these fail-action callback names; materialize against the API event and action state without correcting the standard text.
positive: Enable then disable fail actions and observe the corresponding callbacks.

edge: Contrast with a vacuous success.
positive: Enable nonvacuous actions and complete a property nonvacuously.

edge: Exercise both vacuous and nonvacuous successes after each state change.
positive: Enable then disable pass actions and observe the corresponding callbacks for an assertion.

edge: Use concurrent attempts of the same assertion and distinguish their successful or failed step events.
notes: Step-callback enablement and default state are owned by the assertion-control requirement in 39.5.2.
positive: Enable stepping for one attempt and separately produce a successful step and a failed step, observing the corresponding callback reason.

negative: Attempt to provoke an assertion callback after cbAssertionSysEnd.
positive: Observe system end after all attempts finish, then request an assertion action and verify no effect.

edge: Accept either ordering of cbAssertionSysInitialized relative to cbStartOfSimulation.
negative: Attempt an assertion-specific action before completion of cbAssertionSysInitialized.
notes: Do not require one ordering relative to cbStartOfSimulation.
positive: Register both initialization callbacks and perform an assertion-specific action only after cbAssertionSysInitialized completes.

edge: Repeat suspension and resumption in one run.
positive: Suspend and resume assertion processing and observe cbAssertionSysKill.

notes: Requires support for an action that locks the assertion system.
positive: Register cbAssertionSysLock, trigger a system-control lock, and observe the callback.

edge: Verify an in-progress attempt is not terminated by the stop.
positive: Stop and resume the system twice while an assertion attempt is already executing.

edge: Use system control to delay activation beyond simulation startup.
notes: The delayed-start scenario requires assertion system control.
positive: Observe cbAssertionSysInitialized followed by cbAssertionSysOn and subsequent assertion-attempt processing at normal startup.

edge: Lock then unlock and verify event order.
positive: Register cbAssertionSysUnlock, unlock a previously locked assertion system, and observe the callback.

edge: Contrast with nonvacuous success.
positive: Disable vacuous actions and produce a vacuous success.

edge: Use a clocking expression distinct from another design clock.
positive: Enable clock-step mode on a multicycle assertion and observe one callback at each assertion clock event.

edge: Apply equivalent controls to pending procedural concurrent assertion instances.
positive: Reset a deferred assertion with a pending report and verify it is flushed; disable one and verify its already pending report may mature.

edge: Place the event exactly relative to adjacent global-clock ticks and require the strictly following tick.
negative: Execute the callback at the event time before the next global-clock tick.
positive: Trigger an assertion callback between global-clock ticks and verify delayed execution with the earlier event cb_time.

edge: Use assertions in both top-level and nested scopes.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Invoke vpi_iterate(vpiAssertion, NULL) in a design containing named assertions in multiple scopes and scan their handles.

edge: Use sibling instances with distinct assertion declarations to check instance scoping.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Scan vpiAssertion objects using a selected instance handle and observe that its assertions are returned.

edge: Register separate routines for two supported callback reasons on the same assertion.

positive: Register a routine and distinct user data for a valid assertion handle and supported reason, then cause that event and observe invocation.

edge: Register different routines for multiple assertion-system reasons.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Register a callback with cb_rtn and a supported assertion-system reason and observe invocation at that event.

edge: Use a step containing multiple matched expressions and compare their reported source references.
positive: Produce a successful assertion step with matched expressions and verify that detail identifies those expressions and their source references.

edge: Fail on the first expression and verify that the one-element array identifies that failure point.
negative: Observe an empty expression array for a failing transition.
positive: Cause a failing transition after earlier matched expressions and verify the final array element identifies the failing expression.

edge: Use two distinct paths and verify their source/destination state IDs uniquely identify the path transitions.
positive: Observe step details along a path from origin through an intermediate state to an accepting state and verify the defined state-ID categories.

edge: Contrast an unconditional zero-expression transition with a conditional transition that reports its matched expression.
positive: Construct an unconditional assertion transition and verify that its step detail can contain zero matched expressions.

edge: Use a null user-data value.
notes: A VPI consumer is required.
positive: Register distinct user data and verify the invoked routine receives it with the callback reason.

edge: Use sibling scopes to verify selection.
positive: Apply a control to one scope, then with NULL to all scopes.
End with active attempts and callbacks, then attempt further control and assertion activity.

edge: Repeat disable and enable operations.
positive: Fail assertions before disable, while disabled, and after enable.
Kill active attempts and verify no new attempt starts while callback registrations remain.
Lock, attempt a status change, unlock, and repeat the change.

edge: Enable while an attempt is active, verify that attempt is unaffected, and repeat the enable control.
positive: Enable nonvacuous-success pass actions in one scope and verify a later nonvacuous success executes its pass action.

edge: Verify callback registrations remain.
positive: Turn off while one attempt runs and before another would start.
Turn off or kill, then turn on and observe new attempts with callbacks retained.

edge: Repeat disable and enable operations.
positive: Exercise vacuous and nonvacuous pass actions before disable, while disabled, and after enable.

edge: Verify non-step callbacks survive.
positive: Reset with active attempts and both step and non-step callbacks.

edge: Disable while an attempt is active, verify that attempt is unaffected, and repeat the disable control.
positive: Disable vacuous-success pass actions in one scope and verify a later vacuous success does not execute its pass action.

negative: Attempt to obtain an unnamed assertion using vpi_handle_by_name.

positive: Confirm an unnamed assertion remains available through iteration.

edge: Navigate objects nested below multiple scopes rather than only top-level objects.

positive: Navigate an elaborated design and obtain handles for a named assertion, property, and sequence object.

edge: Use sibling instances containing distinct objects and verify direct iteration remains instance-scoped.

positive: From one elaborated instance handle, directly iterate its assertion, property, and sequence objects.
